source: https://www.kaggle.com/models/google/bird-vocalization-classifier (workbook ID 145, read in Chrome 2026-10-06; card now describes Perch 2.0; no raw file saved)

modelDetails.type: Bioacoustics audio classification and embedding model
modelDetails.architecture: EfficientNet-B3 embedding model with about 12 million parameters plus a species classification head of 91 million parameters; 1536-dimensional embeddings
modelDetails.description: Perch is a bioacoustics model trained to classify nearly 15,000 species and to generate audio embeddings for downstream applications.

intendedUse.primaryIntendedUseCases: Classifying nearly 15,000 species from audio, mostly birds but also frogs, crickets, grasshoppers and mammals; generating audio embeddings for downstream applications such as individual identification and estimating coral reef health; detecting critically endangered birds; powering audio search engines

factors.hardware: The perch_v2 variant requires a GPU; the perch_v2_cpu variant runs on a CPU

evaluation.datasets: Tasks include species classification in avian soundscapes, call type and dialect recognition, individual identification of dogs and bats, and event detection in coral reefs; benchmarks BirdSet and BEANS
evaluation.performance: State-of-the-art scores on bioacoustics benchmarks such as BirdSet and BEANS

trainingData.dataset: Publicly available audio from Xeno-Canto, iNaturalist, Animal Sound Archive and FSD50k
trainingData.procedure: Trained with a softmax head; the softmax is not applied at inference time

ethicalConsiderations.limitations: Output logits for species are uncalibrated and possibly unreliable for rare species

modelCardContent.caveatsAndRecommendations: Tune detection thresholds on your own data; for most cases train a simple linear classifier on top of the embeddings; use an agile modelling workflow with a human annotator in the loop for most bioacoustics applications; the model consumes 5-second audio segments sampled at 32 kHz, so resample audio with other sample rates
